 Live .  42,590 viewing 42590 viewing Live page Updated 4 minutes ago Flights grounded across US as homeland security secretary says no indication of an attack
 FAA Orders Rare Grounding of All US Flights
 BBC News
 Close Watch live Summary
 Flights have been grounded across the US due to an air traffic control communications issue - here's what we know so far 
 There's no indication that this is an attack against the US, the homeland security secretary says, adding that "everybody's safe" - what else did he say? 
 Markwayne Mullin sought to reassure the public, saying repeatedly that this isn't "another 9/11", our Washington correspondent writes 
 US aviation officials earlier issued an order to ground all flights due to "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety"
 Several major airports confirmed the ground stop ; there's currently no indication of when the order will be lifted
 Close form Have you been affected?
 Get in touch Media caption, 'It's going to take some time' - US Homeland Security secretary on nationwide ground stop Live Reporting
 Edited by Dulcie Lee in Washington DC
 Travellers shocked to learn of nationwide grounding published at 23:06 GMT 23:06 GMT 
 Regan Morris 
Reporting from Burbank, California 
 Image caption, Taylor and Jack are among those who have been told their flight might not leave on Friday
 Travellers arriving at Burbank Airport expressed relief they made it to ground safely. 
 Others whose flights were not leaving rushed to the rental car line, which is now stretched around the building. 
 Taylor Brothers and Jack Formisani arrived hours early for their flight and were shocked to be told that they might not be flying back to New York today. "It’s nationwide?" Jack asked. 
 The couple just got engaged and were in Los Angeles so Jack could meet Taylor’s family. 
 "That’s so scary," Taylor said when told all flights were grounded. "I don’t think I want to fly today."

 United says no domestic flights will take off while ground stop in place published at 22:53 GMT 22:53 GMT 
 United Airlines says new domestic flights will not depart while the ground stop remains in place, but international departures are being managed on a case-by-case basis by the FAA. 
 The airlines has advised passengers to check the latest status of their flights or rebook on their website. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 I'm in the air - and we're still due to land in Cleveland published at 22:50 GMT 22:50 GMT 
 Chris Corrall 
Reporting from an Aer Lingus flight 
 I'm currently connected to inflight WiFi on
an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Cleveland, Ohio to see family.
 I found out
about the grounded flights through a message from my wife asking if we were
okay. Shortly after, there was a message from the pilot that all US flights are
grounded. 
 Apparently, some passengers had already seen the news and were
asking if we were going to be impacted.
 Our pilot has since come over the
intercom again to say they've negotiated an earlier landing slot for us, so it
looks like we will still be landing at our destination.

 Flights 'operating normally' north of the border, says Canada air navigation provider published at 22:48 GMT 22:48 GMT 
 Nav Canada, which operates the country's civil air navigation system, says that its systems are "operating normally" and the ground stop in the United States is not affecting flights.
 The company adds that it continues to support the safe movement of planes - "including any aircraft that may be diverted".

 American Airlines says disruption expected to last all day published at 22:42 GMT 22:42 GMT 
 In a statement, American Airlines says flights already in the air will continue to their destinations, but disruptions to the regular schedule are expected for the remainder of the day.
 “It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible once the FAA lifts this nationwide ground stop,” the airline says.

 Image source, Reuters Image caption, People check their phones at New York's John F Kennedy International Airport
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, The flight board at an airport in East Boston, Massachussetts, shows several flights delayed and cancelled

 What we know about the US flight groundstop published at 22:33 GMT 22:33 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters What we know 
 US aviation officials have grounded all flights in the US "due to extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety"
 The US transportation secretary says that a "communication issue" has hit air traffic control centres and that federal aviation technicians are investigating
 Posting on X, the FAA confirms that a "temporary telecommunications outage" is behind today's rare ground stop, adding that "every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis".
 Flight-tracking website Flightrader24 says that there are 3,100 aircraft in the air and bound for US airports, but no additional aircraft are taking off at this time
 Passengers onboard say that flights that have landed are not allowed to move from the tarmac to the gates
 Several major US airports have confirmed the ground stop, advising passengers to contact their airline before heading to the airport
 The Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says that "this isn't another 9/11", seeking to reassure the public 
 Mullin adds that the ground stop is unrelated to the ongoing Microsoft outage
 What we don't know 
 It's unclear how many flights are currently grounded
 It's also unknown what has caused the issue 
 It's unclear how long it will take to resolve the problem

 US air traffic control is notoriously antiquated published at 22:29 GMT 22:29 GMT 
 Theo Leggett 
International business correspondent 
 We don’t know exactly what has caused the current issue,
but US air traffic control systems are notoriously antiquated. 
 Last year,
Congress approved $12.5bn (£9.5bn) for upgrades, but much more is needed.
 Just a couple of weeks ago, the Federal Aviation
Administration pledged to replace systems that still rely on floppy discs - a
form of local data storage that was commonplace in the 1980s and 90s - by the
end of 2028.

 Every flight accounted for - FAA published at 22:28 GMT 22:28 GMT 
 Posting on X, US aviation officials confirm that a "temporary telecommunications outage" is behind today's rare ground stop. 
 "There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted," the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says. 
 "Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Flight crew seems 'to be unaware of what's going on', says stranded passenger published at 22:24 GMT 22:24 GMT 
 Micah Feinstein is on a plane at Baltimore/Washington International Airport trying to travel to Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil.
 He tells the BBC his flight was about to take off when passengers were informed they would be unable to leave. 
 There's been little communication from the crew, he adds, and they seem "to be unaware of what's going on".
 "We the passengers are equally as confused," Micah says. "Folks have been pretty calm. I think we're all just... trying to sort out our plans."
 Micah says he himself will need to find a solution as he's expecting to miss his connecting flight from Panama City - if he manages to take off at all from Maryland.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 US seeks to reassure public - but there are more questions than answers published at 22:22 GMT 22:22 GMT 
 Daniel Bush 
Washington correspondent 
 Image source, Reuters US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has just sought to reassure the public that the nationwide air traffic outage wasn't caused by a "nefarious act".
 He said repeatedly that this "isn’t another 9/11".
 But beyond that, he made clear there are more questions than answers about what's going on.
 The administration is working to address what he said was a "telecommunications outage". But he acknowledged the government doesn't know what caused it or how long it'll take to fix.
 Mullin also said that he couldn’t "rule anything out" as a reason for the outage, despite saying that there was no current indication of an attack.
 It's worth noting that up until now Mullin has been best known for overseeing a ramp-up of the administration’s immigration deportation program. This crisis will test his leadership atop the agency in charge of protecting the US homeland.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'There's some confusion' - BBC presenter stuck at Denver Airport published at 22:15 GMT 22:15 GMT 
 The BBC's Chief Presenter Sumi Somaskanda recently arrived at Denver Airport and says "there's some confusion" there.
 She says the screens at the airport announcing when flights are leaving haven't caught up following news of the ground stop. 
 "You have a number of people here who are checking in bags, who are going to the counters to try and get ready for their flights and head over to security but they're now hearing there's a groundstop."
 Among those also at the airport is US Congressman Ro Khanna, who was at a Democratic conference that the BBC was reporting on. 
 Somaskanda says that while people have started to gather, "it's going to become very chaotic as more and more people realise that none of these flights are going anywhere". 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What we learned from the homeland security secretary published at 22:12 GMT 22:12 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters We've just heard from Markwayne Mullin, who leads the US Department of Homeland Security. He says:
 A "telecommunications outage" has led to the ground stop 
 The Federal Aviation Administration has grounded all flights "out of an abundance of caution"
 He tells journalists gathered at the White House that everybody is safe, all flights are accounted for and "there should be no fear to the public at all"
 "This isn't another 9/11," he says. "This is a telecommunication outage, this is much different"
 He adds that there is no reason to connect today's issues to the ongoing Microsoft outage
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Issue not connected to Microsoft outage - Mullin published at 22:08 GMT 22:08 GMT 
 Mullin says the focus at the moment is on restoring communication and to "get all the flights down" on the ground.
 He adds there isn't "any reason" to connect today's issues with Microsoft and the current outage.
 "We have not discussed any time frame," he says when asked about the potential length of the issues.
 "It's going to take some time."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Everybody's safe' - Mullin published at 22:05 GMT 22:05 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters "Everybody's safe," the homeland security secretary adds, saying this isn't "another 9/11".
 He recalls that the last time a national groundstop was issued was during the 9/11 attacks in 2001, before adding this isn't "another 9/11".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 No indication of an attack - homeland security secretary published at 22:03 GMT 22:03 GMT Breaking 
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is speaking to reporters at the White House now.
 He says there is no indication this was an attack against the United States. 
 "This is a telecommunications outage," he says.
 "All the flights are accounted for," he says.
 Media caption, 'It's going to take some time' - US Homeland Security secretary on nationwide ground stop

 Several airports confirm ground stop published at 21:45 GMT 21:45 GMT Breaking 
 Several airports have confirmed flights have been grounded after the FAA's announcement, with many advising passengers to check their flight status directly with their airline.
 Those issuing statements include:
 Atlanta Airport , external 
 Washington DC's Reagan Airport , external 
 Miami International Airport , external 
 BWI Marshall Airport , external 
 George Bush Intercontinental Airport , external 
 The FAA adds that a ground stop and delays are possible at:
 LA International Airport (LAX)
 Harry Reid International in Las Vegas
 JFK
 Philadelphia International

 Passenger tells of people stuck on plane in Los Angeles published at 21:41 GMT 21:41 GMT 
 A passenger stuck on a plane at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) says flights which have just landed are not being allowed to move from the tarmac to the gates.
 The passenger, who has travelled from Newark, tells the BBC's US partner CBS News that they're unable to taxi to the gate as another plane scheduled to take off is not being allowed to depart.
 Another passenger who just landed in Austin tells the broadcaster he and fellow travellers have been told they should "sit tight" as they're also unable to leave the plane.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 More than 3,000 flights currently bound for US airports - Flightradar24 published at 21:34 GMT 21:34 GMT Breaking 
 Image source, Flightradar24 Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 says 3,100 airborne aircraft are currently bound for US airports. 
 On X, it says that no additional aircraft are taking off at this time.
 In its statement, the FAA said inbound international flights would be managed on a "case by case basis".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Transport secretary says 'communication issue' has hit traffic control centres published at 21:23 GMT 21:23 GMT Breaking 
 Transport Secretary Sean Duffy says the FAA "issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.
 "FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them," he says.
